stem: A company needs an encrypted connection between its headquarters and its AWS VPC within the next two days to support a time-limited project, and it can tolerate the variable latency of a connection that runs over the public internet. Which option fits?

choices.text: AWS Direct Connect, provisioned through a Direct Connect partner
AWS Site-to-Site VPN between a customer gateway and a virtual private gateway
An interface endpoint for the specific AWS services headquarters needs to reach
A NAT gateway configured to accept inbound connections from headquarters

rationale: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an IPsec-encrypted connection over the public internet between a customer gateway and a virtual private gateway or transit gateway, and it is quick to provision, which fits both the two-day deadline and the tolerance for internet-path latency. Direct Connect typically requires a colocation facility or a Direct Connect partner and takes considerably longer to provision, which does not fit a two-day deadline. An interface endpoint connects a VPC to individual AWS services over PrivateLink; it does not provide connectivity between an entire on-premises headquarters network and a VPC. A NAT gateway only supports outbound-initiated connections from resources inside the VPC and provides no encryption and no mechanism for headquarters to initiate an inbound connection, so it cannot serve as a site-to-site link at all.
